claims.text: A high-alkalinity, low-temperature synthesis regime with Pd-, Rh-, and Ga-enriched composition selection promotes controlled post-ageing electronic and atomic reconstruction.
Post-ageing reconstruction produces electronically coupled Cu–Pt cooperative sites.
Post-ageing reconstruction produces favorable alloy/support interfacial states.
The reconstructed sites overcome activity loss and durability limitations while maintaining low platinum-group-metal consumption.
The starting candidates have a total metal loading of 1 wt%, use up to 19 metal precursors, and are supported on La-doped γ-Al2O3.
Fresh starting catalysts contain agglomerates of fine metallic particles.
The proposed campaign combines automated continuous-solvothermal synthesis, post-ageing screening, machine-learning prediction, Bayesian optimization, and direct inverse analysis.
The proposed synthesis space is 200–350 °C and 20–35 MPa, with alkalinity controlled through precursor, reductant, and 25 M NaOH flow rates.
The intervention selects catalyst compositions enriched in Pd, Rh, and Ga.
The accelerated-ageing protocol uses 900 °C for 5 h under cyclic lean/rich, water-containing gas, followed by oxidizing and reducing treatments at 500 °C.
Light-off performance is tested from 100 to 500 °C in a near-stoichiometric feed containing NO, CO, hydrocarbons, CO2, O2, H2, and N2.
Electronic redistribution during ageing causes beneficial Cu–Pt surface rearrangements.
Cu–Pt cooperative sites weaken overly strong CO binding.
Cu–Pt cooperative sites enhance redox buffering and oxygen mobility.
Pt coordination with Ni or Fe is associated with catalyst deactivation.
Controlled synthesis suppresses detrimental phase segregation.
Favorable alloy/support interactions maintain active sites during transient and low-temperature operation.

After ageing, inverse-model-guided catalysts will achieve at least a 5 °C lower T50 or at least a 2 percentage-point higher conversion at 350 °C than the Pd/Al2O3 benchmark and randomly synthesized catalysts.
Relationships between nanoscale segregation and activity are only qualitatively assigned from ex situ characterization.
Observed electronic-redistribution trends support the proposed Cu–Pt cooperative-site mechanism.
